metadataReview.note: Khmelkov, a participant, describes the German chlorine–bromine gas assault on Osowiec at 04:00 on 6 August 1915 and the counterattack of the 226th Zemlyansky Regiment, whose 13th company charged men of the 18th Landwehr Regiment beside the railway; by 11:00 the Sosnenskaya position was cleared. The atlas point is the heritage-registered Zarechnaya position of the fortress, from which the counterattack companies were sent; it is a sector reference and does not locate the forward trenches or any exact company position. The existing date is retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred; the monograph’s casualty statements are not adopted.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: The NID heritage-register entry “pozycja zarzeczna” (defensive architecture, 1882–1892, Osowiec-Twierdza 8a; INSPIRE id PL.1.9.ZIPOZ.NID_N_20_BL.18711) publishes the map point latitude 53.485486608183, longitude 22.632117036248, rounded to [22.6321,53.4855]. Khmelkov (1939, ch. 4) states that the chief of the 2nd defence section sent the 8th, 13th and 14th companies of the 226th Zemlyansky Regiment from the Zarechnaya position to counterattack, and that this position was the objective of the German assault columns. The point therefore marks the registered position from which the counterattack set out. It is not the Sosnenskaya forward position, which Khmelkov (ch. 2) places 3–3.5 km north-west of the fortress place d’armes between Białogrądy and Sośnia, where the 13th company charged beside the railway; no published coordinate for that line was found. The register does not state how its point was derived, and no accuracy radius is claimed.
